issues.title: Improve Movement Type System for Better User Understanding
issues.body:
## Problem
Current movement types (D/S/T/M) are cryptic and hard for users to understand. Users need clearer guidance on how to categorize movements for accurate calculations.

## Solution
- [ ] Replace cryptic single letters with descriptive names
  - D (Dynamic) → "Gets Harder Over Time"
  - S (Static) → "Consistent Pace"
  - T (Transition) → "Rest/Setup Time" 
  - M (Max) → "Max Reps in Time"
- [ ] Add tooltips/help text explaining when to use each type
- [ ] Include examples for common movements in each category
- [ ] Update movement library with better type guidance
- [ ] Add validation to warn users about questionable type selections

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Help documentation clearly explains each type
- [ ] Existing calculations remain accurate
- [ ] UI provides contextual guidance

issues.title: Add Movement-Specific Fatigue Multipliers
issues.body:
## Problem
Current system applies a uniform fatigue multiplier to all Dynamic movements. Different movements fatigue at different rates and should have individual multipliers.

## Solution
- [ ] Add `fatigue_multiplier` field to movement definitions
- [ ] Update calculation engine to use movement-specific multipliers
- [ ] Research and implement realistic multipliers for common movements:
  - Thrusters: Higher fatigue (1.8-2.2)
  - Wall Balls: Moderate fatigue (1.4-1.6) 
  - Push-ups: Lower fatigue (1.2-1.4)
  - Rowing: Minimal fatigue (1.05-1.1)
- [ ] Allow users to customize multipliers in advanced mode
- [ ] Update movement library with researched multiplier values

## Technical Requirements
- Modify `calculate_movement_totals()` in `src/calculations.py`
- Update movement JSON schema to include multiplier field
- Ensure backward compatibility with existing movements

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Calculations are more accurate for multi-movement workouts
- [ ] Multipliers can be customized per movement
- [ ] Default values provide realistic fatigue modeling
- [ ] Advanced users can fine-tune for personal performance

issues.title: Simplify Transition Management in Live Workout Editor
issues.body:
## Problem
Transition movements (type 'T') in the live workout editor are confusing and cumbersome to manage. Users struggle with understanding their purpose and setting them up correctly.

## Current Issues
- [ ] Transition movements appear in workout calculations but don't contribute to score
- [ ] Users don't understand when/why to use transitions
- [ ] Setting up transition times is not intuitive
- [ ] Transitions clutter the movement list unnecessarily

## Solution

### Simplified Transition Handling
- [ ] Auto-detect common transition scenarios (between different equipment/areas)
- [ ] Provide preset transition times ("Quick change: 10s", "Equipment setup: 30s", "Station move: 45s")
- [ ] Option to add transitions with single click between movements
- [ ] Visual separation of transitions from scored movements

### UI Improvements
- [ ] Collapse/minimize transition display in movement list
- [ ] Add transition time as a simple "+30s rest" indicator
- [ ] Provide transition time suggestions based on movement changes
- [ ] Make transitions optional/toggleable per workout

### Smart Defaults
- [ ] Auto-suggest transitions when switching between:
  - Barbell to bodyweight movements
  - Floor to pull-up bar
  - Different cardio equipment
- [ ] Learn from user patterns to improve suggestions

## Technical Implementation
- [ ] Add transition detection algorithms
- [ ] Create preset transition templates
- [ ] Simplify transition UI components
- [ ] Add transition recommendation engine

## User Experience
- [ ] "I want to add 30 seconds between rounds for equipment setup"
- [ ] "This workout needs time to move from rower to barbell"
- [ ] "Hide transition details but keep the time in calculations"

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Transitions are easy to add and understand
- [ ] UI is cleaner and less cluttered
- [ ] Transition times are realistic and helpful
- [ ] Advanced users can still customize fully
- [ ] New users aren't confused by transition complexity

issues.body:
## Phase 2: Database Migration

Implement comprehensive data validation for database integrity and application reliability.

- [ ] Create input validation for all API endpoints
- [ ] Implement database constraint validation
- [ ] Add business logic validation rules
- [ ] Create data consistency checks

### Validation Layers

#### Input Validation
- API request parameter validation
- Type checking and format validation
- Range validation for numeric inputs
- Required field validation

#### Database Validation
- Foreign key constraint validation
- Unique constraint enforcement
- Check constraint validation (positive times, valid types)
- Data type validation

#### Business Logic Validation
- Movement type consistency (S/D/T/M)
- Workout configuration validation
- Movement-workout compatibility checks
- Execution time reasonableness checks

### Validation Rules

#### Workout Validation
- Total time must be positive
- Multiplier must be > 0
- Rounds must be >= 1
- Time cap must be > total estimated time (warning)

#### Movement Validation
- Execution times must be positive
- Movement types must be S, D, T, or M
- Variety names must be consistent within movement
- Category references must exist

### Error Handling
- [ ] Standardized error response format
- [ ] User-friendly error messages
- [ ] Developer debugging information
- [ ] Error logging and monitoring
- [ ] Graceful degradation for non-critical errors

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All validation rules implemented and tested
- [ ] Comprehensive test coverage for edge cases
- [ ] Clear error messages for users
- [ ] Performance impact minimized
- [ ] Integration with existing error handling

### Dependencies

issues.title: [ROADMAP] Django Models Implementation
issues.body:
## Phase 3: Django Backend

### Goal
Implement Django models that map to the database schema with proper relationships and validation.

### Technical Requirements
- [ ] Create Category model with metadata
- [ ] Create Movement model with varieties relationship
- [ ] Create MovementVariety model with execution times
- [ ] Create Workout model with configuration
- [ ] Create WorkoutMovement through model for many-to-many
- [ ] Add model validation and custom methods

### Model Specifications

#### Category Model
- Fields: key, name, description, icon, category_type
- Methods: `__str__()`, `get_workouts()`, `get_movements()`
- Validation: unique key, valid category_type

#### Movement Model
- Fields: name, slug, category, movement_type, base_execution_time
- Relationships: ForeignKey to Category, OneToMany to MovementVariety
- Methods: `get_execution_time(variety)`, `get_varieties()`
- Validation: valid movement_type (S/D/T/M), positive execution time

#### MovementVariety Model
- Fields: movement, name, execution_time, scaling_notes, is_default
- Relationships: ForeignKey to Movement
- Methods: `__str__()`, `get_scaling_info()`
- Validation: positive execution_time, one default per movement

#### Workout Model
- Fields: name, slug, description, category, workout_type, total_time, etc.
- Relationships: ManyToMany to Movement through WorkoutMovement
- Methods: `calculate_estimated_time()`, `get_movement_list()`
- Validation: positive times, valid workout_type

#### WorkoutMovement Model (Through Table)
- Fields: workout, movement, variety, count, order_position
- Methods: `get_movement_display()`, `calculate_time()`
- Validation: positive count (or -1 for max), valid order

### Django Features
- [ ] Model admin customization
- [ ] Custom model managers and querysets
- [ ] Model serialization for API
- [ ] Database migration files
- [ ] Model unit tests

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All models pass validation tests
- [ ] Relationships work correctly
- [ ] Admin interface provides full CRUD functionality
- [ ] Models integrate with existing data migration
- [ ] Performance is acceptable for expected data volumes

### Dependencies

- Uses database schema design
- Foundation for REST API development

issues.title: Add Elite/RX+/RX/Scaled Performance Labeling
issues.body:
## Goal
Provide performance context by labeling workout times and movement paces with appropriate skill levels.

## Performance Levels

### Elite (Top 1-5%)
- Competition-level athletes
- Games/Regionals qualifiers
- Professional/sponsored athletes

### RX+ (Top 10-20%)
- Advanced recreational athletes
- Local competition winners
- Consistent RX performers

### RX (Standard)
- Prescribed workout as written
- Competent in all movement patterns
- Can complete workouts safely at intended stimulus

### Scaled (Entry Level)
- Modified movements/loads
- Skill development focus
- Maintains workout stimulus with adaptations

## Implementation

### Movement Pace Labeling
- [ ] Add performance level indicators to movement library
- [ ] Show user's pace level for each movement
- [ ] Provide progression targets (scaled → RX → RX+ → Elite)

### Workout Result Labeling
- [ ] Compare user times to performance benchmarks
- [ ] Display performance level achieved
- [ ] Show percentile ranking where data available

### Benchmark Data Collection
- [ ] Research elite performance times
- [ ] Collect community performance data
- [ ] Establish statistical benchmarks
- [ ] Update benchmarks with new data

## UI Features
- [ ] Performance level badges/indicators
- [ ] Progress tracking toward next level
- [ ] Benchmark comparison charts
- [ ] Goal setting based on performance levels

## Data Structure
```json
{
  "benchmarks": {
    "scaled": {"time": "15:00", "percentile": 25},
    "rx": {"time": "10:00", "percentile": 50},
    "rxplus": {"time": "8:00", "percentile": 80},
    "elite": {"time": "6:00", "percentile": 95}
  }
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Performance levels accurately reflect fitness community standards
- [ ] Users understand their current performance level
- [ ] Progression paths are clear and motivating
- [ ] Benchmarks are updated with real performance data
